title: Is Angi Worth It? The Real Math Two Tradesmen Ran
h1: Is Angi Worth It? We Ran the Real Math
meta: Is Angi worth it for contractors? The honest cost-per-booked-job math: a shared lead is sold to up to 12 pros, and 78% of homeowners hire whoever calls first (Lead Connect 2026).
short: For most shops, no. A shared Angi lead gets sold to as many as 12 pros, so the true cost isn't the lead price — it's the lead price divided by a brutal close rate. Run cost per booked job, not cost per lead.
statLabel: Pros your 'exclusive' Angi lead can be sold to — the number that wrecks the math

body.answer: A shared lead sold to a dozen pros is a race, not a customer.
body.html: Angi can work — for a specific kind of shop, in a specific situation. For everybody else it quietly bleeds money, because the price on the screen isn't the price you pay. A shared lead is sold to up to 12 pros at once, so you're not buying a job. You're buying an at-bat against eleven other trucks.

body.h2: Cost per lead is the lie. Cost per booked job is the truth.
body.answer: Divide the lead price by your close rate on shared leads — that's your real number.
body.html: Say a lead runs $35. Feels cheap. But on a shared lead you're one of many, and 78% of homeowners hire whoever responds first (Lead Connect 2026). If you close one in twelve, that '$35 lead' just became a few hundred dollars per booked job — before you've unrolled a tarp. We won't hand you a fake industry average here; run your close rate on shared leads and do the division. The answer usually stings.

body.answer: New shop, no pipeline, and you answer the phone in seconds.
body.html: There's one honest case: you're brand new, you have zero pipeline, and you will pick up on the first ring every single time. Speed is everything — responding in 5 minutes instead of 30 makes you up to 100x more likely to connect (MIT Sloan 2026). If that's not you, the money is better spent owning your own presence.

body.html: Marshall and Ray went deep on this in Is Angi Worth It? on Get Booked, Not F***ed — same math, more cussing. Watch or listen to the full episode here.

faq.q: Is Angi worth it for a new contractor?
faq.a: It can bridge a gap if you have no pipeline and answer instantly — 78% of homeowners hire whoever responds first (Lead Connect 2026). Long term, owning your own leads is cheaper per booked job.

faq.q: Why is a shared lead so expensive if it's cheap?
faq.a: Because it's sold to up to 12 pros. The low price is per lead; your real cost is per booked job, which is the lead price divided by a low shared-lead close rate.

faq.q: What should I do instead of Angi?
faq.a: Own your Google Business Profile, systematize referrals, and capture the homeowners already on your website. Those leads are exclusive and don't vanish when you stop paying.
